arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22: she texted about the dog-faced man, he sent the Moshe photo the same day. Mon Nov 23: aphids on Moshe; he phones her at the café; 'soap, water, gently. Wednesday I'll inspect him... and we talk.' Next: midpoint Wed Nov 25, Lior lets it slip before she can.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22: 'the system ate November', 'Thursday-ish' by email; the Ruti reply sits in drafts. Mon Nov 23: Gadi phones for a 'tiny' Hanukkah banner by tonight, no fee; Ishai: 'After Thursday.' Gadi laughs too long, mentions 'other agencies are crying, not us'. Next: Thursday comes; week 3 Gadi asks for January.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22: phoned from a flat that echoes ('feng shui'). Mon Nov 23: Tomer fixes her socket and phones Ishai from the street: one toothbrush, half the shelves empty, 'minimalism'. Tomer: 'Ask her. Not me. You.' Ishai: 'Saturday.' Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19 ('I want to be paid for what I already did'). Mon Nov 23 he uses it on Gadi's banner: 'After Thursday.' Lesson 4 Thu Nov 26, the last one Noa paid for.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22: the date story with the cats' breakfast; Moti: 'nobody is that busy; why doesn't SHE call?' Mon Nov 23: Moti on the stairs before poker, the committee folder and Eli's old stair light. Next: Thu Nov 26 revealed; week 3 Ishai quietly messages Eli.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22: Ishai finally asks about the envelope and the proverbs. Avi: 'January is always bad'; he'll tell him after the poker night; one proverb: 'the oil doesn't care what January says'. Next: the telling (Tue/Wed).
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Wed: chapter thirteen, the coat for a cold city; 'up north'. Fri: chapter fourteen, 'the barista practises the names of streets she has never walked'; asks Ishai if he knows streets up north. Ishai still doesn't recognise himself ('the man in your book sounds like a pushover'). Sun: no café visit.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Sat: phoned Ishai three times about the date ('for science'); Noa dodges his texts. Mon Nov 23: he goes to Noa's to look at a socket (she told Ishai Sunday night). Next: showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat Nov 21: 'listen to what she doesn't say'; 'ask where she is tonight' (Ishai asked it in the park, it worked). Next: Ishai tells him how it went.

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22 at Avi's: Boaz checks 'eight, fifty, small notes', warns about Ronit; Yossi meets Ishai, the cap 'on holiday since summer', tells him to bring 'a little extra, for emergencies'. Moti: don't sit next to the cap. First night Mon Nov 23 (engine). After it: Yossi asks Ishai to lend him 200.
arcs.secret: Yossi is broke: the lucky cap hasn't paid in months, and he owes money at the depot.

beats.goal: Back from the morning walk, Ishai finds tiny green bugs under Moshe's leaves: aphids. Panic, then a photo to Dana. She texts back from the café, he phones her. She is warm and practical (soap and water, gently, no poison near the sprout) and says Wednesday she'll come and inspect Moshe herself, 'and we talk'. Something in her voice is careful. No secret is told.
beats.teaser: Moshe has visitors. Tiny green ones. Ishai calls the expert.
beats.forceText: Ishai finds aphids on Moshe and phones Dana; she tells him soap and water and says Wednesday she'll inspect him, 'and we talk'.

forceLines.say: Soap and water. Gently. Wednesday I inspect him.
And we talk. You said that twice now.

forceCommentary.say: Moshe has aphids. I'd like a moment. I'm not okay.
A plant emergency as an excuse to call her. Moshe, you wingman.

moments.text: Ishai bends over Moshe on the counter by the sink, turns a leaf over and freezes: tiny green dots, dozens of them. He takes a photo, close.

lines.say: Moshe. Who are your friends? Those are not friends.
Okay. Don't panic. I'm asking the expert.

commentary.say: Moshe has aphids. Nobody speak to me for the rest of the hour.
He sent the photo in nine seconds. For Dana, he's fast now.

message.say: Aphids. Don't you dare spray anything. Call me, I have two minutes.

moments.text: Her text lights up the phone almost at once. He reads it out loud, then calls her; behind her voice, the café's milk steamer.

lines.say: 'Don't you dare spray anything.' She knows me.
Two minutes. The queue is out the door.
He has bugs. Little green ones. Under every leaf.
Aphids. They love new leaves. It means he's growing.
So it's a compliment?
It's a party. Somebody has to end it.
How?
Warm water, a drop of dish soap. Wipe the leaves. Gently.
Gently. I can do gently.
Not the sprout. Move the sprout away. Today.
Quarantine. Got it.
Wednesday I'll come and inspect him myself.
After the Pump House?
Before. And... we talk. Properly.
You keep saying that like it's a test.
It's not a test. It's just... Wednesday. Go wipe leaves.

commentary.say: 'And we talk. Properly.' Second time she's said it. I'm counting too now.
Warm water, one drop of soap. Finally someone on this show gives clear instructions.

update.memory: Ishai phoned about aphids on Moshe. Told him soap and water, move the sprout. Said Wednesday I'll inspect Moshe, and we talk. Properly.

moments.text: At the sink Ishai wipes Moshe's leaves one by one with a wet cloth, slowly, then carries the little sprout to the far end of the counter.

lines.say: Gently. Like she said. Sorry, Moshe. No, not sorry. Gently.
You stay over there. Quarantine. It's for your own good.

commentary.say: Leaf by leaf. If he wiped a stranger's face this gently, he'd be arrested. Lovingly.
He caught his own sorry. To a plant. Improv works, people.

beats.goal: Gadi phones all cheer: a client needs a 'tiny' Hanukkah banner by tonight, eight candles, 'twenty minutes for you', no word about a fee or Thursday. Ishai, at his desk, uses the improv: 'Yes, and after Thursday.' Gadi laughs too long, says other agencies are crying this year 'but not us', and hangs up fast. Ishai sits with it; opens the Ruti draft, doesn't send.
beats.teaser: Gadi needs 'one tiny banner'. Tonight. Guess who's paying.
beats.forceText: Gadi phones for a tiny Hanukkah banner by tonight; Ishai says he'll do it after Thursday's payment.

forceLines.say: Twenty minutes for you! Eight candles, a little glow.

forceCommentary.say: 'Yes, and after Thursday.' Somebody frame that sentence.
Gadi laughed for eleven seconds. I timed it. Nobody laughs that long at good news.

moments.text: Ishai at his desk, a half-finished layout on the screen. The phone rings: Gadi. He lets it ring twice, then answers.

lines.say: Ishai! My Hanukkah hero! Quick one, tiny.
Hi, Gadi. How tiny?
A banner. Eight candles, a little glow, a dreidel maybe.
For who?
A client. A good one. Tonight, for the website.
Tonight.
Twenty minutes for you! You're fast. You're the fastest.
Gadi, what about Thursday?
Thursday is Thursday. This is Monday!
Yes. I'll do the banner.
See? Team!
Yes, and I'll do it after Thursday.
After... ha. Ha ha. You're funny now.
I'm not joking. After the money. Then the candles.
Ishai. Every agency is crying this year. Not us.
Then Thursday is easy.
Ha! Okay. Okay. I'll... call you. Bye, hero.

commentary.say: Eight candles, a little glow, a dreidel maybe. And a fee? Maybe never.
'Every agency is crying. Not us.' Gadi, darling, why bring up the crying?

update.memory: Asked Ishai for a tiny Hanukkah banner tonight. He said yes, after Thursday's money. Laughed it off. Said other agencies are crying, not us.

moments.text: The call ends. Ishai looks at the phone for a long moment, then opens his drafts: the reply to Ruti from Thursday. He reads it, his hand over the mouse.

lines.say: 'Every agency is crying.' Why would he say that?
Not today. But not never.

commentary.say: The Ruti draft. Open. Not sent. The longest foreplay in email history.
He said no to Gadi and didn't say sorry. Somewhere a toaster is proud.

beats.goal: Dusk walk in the park with Falafel. Tomer phones from the street outside Noa's after fixing her socket. He's loud as always but uneasy: the flat is half empty, one toothbrush, a bare wall where the big photo hung, she called it minimalism and pushed him out with a cold drink in ten minutes. He doesn't know why (he must not guess the truth); he wants Ishai to ask her: 'not me, you, you're her person'. Ishai promises to ask Saturday. A flash of how much Tomer cares about Noa.
beats.teaser: Tomer fixed Noa's socket. Now he has questions about her flat.
beats.forceText: Tomer phones Ishai after fixing Noa's socket: her flat is half empty and she called it minimalism; he wants Ishai to ask her.

forceLines.say: One toothbrush, man. She called it minimalism.

forceCommentary.say: Tomer noticed the toothbrush. Tomer notices everything about Noa. Interesting.
An electrician who checks the bathroom. Thorough. Suspiciously thorough.

moments.text: Late afternoon in the park, the light going gold over the pond. Ishai walks Falafel on the short leash; the duck keeps a careful distance.

lines.say: Falafel, the duck is not a snack. We've talked about this.

commentary.say: Sunset, a dog, a duck. The most peaceful three minutes this man will have all day.
Poker in four hours. He's walking it off before it starts.

moments.text: By the bench his phone rings: Tomer, traffic and a bus behind him. He sounds like himself, only quieter at the end of every sentence.

lines.say: Socket's done. Twenty minutes. I'm a genius.
Noa's? How's the flat?
That's why I'm calling. Bro. It's empty.
Empty how?
Half the shelves. A nail on the wall, no picture.
She said feng shui.
She said minimalism to me. Same face.
Maybe she's redecorating.
One toothbrush, Ishai. One. I checked. I'm an electrician.
Electricians check toothbrushes?
Bathroom socket. I saw. Don't change the subject.
Did you ask her?
She gave me a cold drink and pushed me out in ten minutes.
That's... very Noa lately.
Not me asking. You. You're her person.
Saturday. I'll ask her properly. Not on the phone.
Saturday. Good. And Ishai... look after her a bit, yeah?
Since when do you say things like that?
Since never. Forget it. Win tonight, loser.

commentary.say: 'Look after her a bit.' Tomer. TOMER. Sweetheart, what's going on there?
He checked the toothbrushes. For the socket. Obviously.

update.memory: Fixed Noa's socket. Her flat is half empty, one toothbrush. Told Ishai to ask her, not me. He promised Saturday. Asked him to look after her.

moments.text: The call over, Ishai sits on the bench a while, phone in hand, Falafel's head on his shoe. He types to Noa, deletes it, types again.

lines.say: 'Saturday. Dinner. Just us. No plumbers.' Send.
Nail on the wall, no picture...

commentary.say: Typed, deleted, typed. The man drafts texts like peace treaties.
'No plumbers.' Oh, he knows something's off. He just doesn't know what.

beats.goal: Before poker: Ishai goes to the Tahini Tower ATM on the shops block for fifty in small notes, and remembers Yossi's 'a little extra for emergencies', so he takes out a little more. A text from Dana: 'Don't apologise to the chips.' Avi at the kiosk, wiping down, says 'tomorrow, the envelope', and wishes him luck. Home on the stairs Moti, with the committee folder and his own small notes, coaches him on the table: Ronit reads faces, keep yours boring, and don't lend money at the table. Ishai is back in the flat by 19:20, well before eight.
beats.teaser: Small notes, one ATM, and Dana's advice before Ishai's first poker night.
beats.forceText: Ishai takes out small notes at the ATM before poker; Moti warns him on the stairs that Ronit reads faces and nobody lends at the table.

forceLines.say: Ronit reads faces. Keep yours boring.
I have the most boring face in the building.

forceCommentary.say: Dana texted 'don't apologise to the chips'. She knows him. She KNOWS him.
Moti brought his own small notes. Folded by value. Of course.

message.say: Good luck tonight. Don't apologise to the chips. How's the patient?

moments.text: Evening on the shops block, the crossing lights ticking. Ishai at the Tahini Tower ATM: fifty in small notes, then he stops and adds a little more. Dana's text arrives as the machine counts.

lines.say: 'Don't apologise to the chips.' Ha. No promises.
A little extra. For emergencies. Whose emergencies?

commentary.say: She remembered poker night. She asked about Moshe. Wednesday can't come fast enough.
He took out extra because a stranger in a cap told him to. Financial planning, Ishai-style.

moments.text: Back on Herzl Street Avi is wiping down the counter, the lawyer's envelope still under the calculator by the tahini. He waves Ishai over.

lines.say: Champion! Tonight the cards, yes?
Eight o'clock. Small notes. I'm ready.
Nobody is ready for Ronit. She took my watch once.
Your watch?
Not really. Felt like it.
And tomorrow? The envelope?
Tomorrow. I said after your card game. I keep my word.
Is it bad?
It's paper, champion. Paper is always bad.
That's not a proverb.
No. Proverbs I'll find again. Maybe January.
Tomorrow, then. I'll bring coffee.
Bring luck. Leave the coffee. Go. Win something.

commentary.say: 'Paper is always bad.' Avi's proverbs are getting worse. That's the bad sign.
Tomorrow, the envelope. Tonight, the cards. Busy week, champion.

update.memory: Wished Ishai luck before his poker night. Promised again: tomorrow I'll tell him about the envelope. He'll bring coffee.

moments.text: On the stairs Moti comes up from the mailboxes with the committee folder and a neat stack of small notes held with a clip. He stops Ishai with one finger.

lines.say: Neighbour. Small notes?
Fifty. And a bit.
Why a bit?
Yossi said for emergencies.
Hm. Yossi says many things.
What do I need to know?
Ronit reads faces. Keep yours boring.
I have the most boring face in the building.
Boaz plays slow. Don't hurry him. He hates hurry.
And Yossi?
Yossi you watch. And one rule: nobody lends at the table.
Why would anyone—
It's a rule. Rules exist because once, someone did. Eight sharp.
Eight sharp. Thanks, Moti.

commentary.say: 'Nobody lends at the table.' Moti, why so specific? Who did what?
Moti clipped his poker money. With a committee clip. I respect it.

update.memory: Coached Ishai on the stairs before his first poker night: Ronit reads faces, Boaz plays slow, watch Yossi, nobody lends at the table.

hook.text: 'A little extra, for emergencies,' and 'nobody lends at the table.' First poker night at Boaz's. Whose emergency is it?

previously.text: Noa's flat echoes; she says she has to 'get used to it'. Tomer goes there today to fix a socket. Get used to what? Nobody said.

hosts: Monday. Poker night. Ishai has never played for money. Ishai has never played.
Fifty shekels in small notes. The most organised gambler in Tel Aviv.
Boaz calls him 'the quiet one'. Tonight we find out if quiet is a strategy.
Ronit is a maths teacher. She grades bluffs. Harshly.
Yossi's lucky cap has been 'on holiday' since summer. Where does a cap go on holiday?
Moshe update: new leaves, which is good. New guests, which is not.
Dana said 'we talk' on Saturday. Wednesday is two days away. Ishai has checked the calendar four times.
Gadi's payment is 'Thursday-ish'. The '-ish' is doing a lot of work.
The Ruti draft is still in drafts. Drafts are where courage goes to nap.
Tomer is at Noa's today with a screwdriver. Tomer always has a screwdriver.
Noa called her flat feng shui. Oren looked it up. Feng shui doesn't echo.
Seventeen degrees and partly cloudy. Perfect weather for losing fifty shekels.
Falafel doesn't play poker. Falafel doesn't need to. He wins every staring contest.
Ben-Gurion the cat had breakfast before Ishai did. Again.
Mrs. Levi's cough is quieter today. Her opinions, not quieter.
Avi said he'd explain the envelope 'after the card game'. That's tomorrow. Mark it.
Moti has the committee folder. Moti always has the committee folder.
Poker rule one: don't apologise when you win. Ishai's rule one: apologise.
Boaz drives line 88 all day and hosts poker at night. When does the man sit still? Oh. Poker.
Oren's prediction: Ishai folds a winning hand to be polite.
Zohar's prediction: Ishai wins one big pot and says sorry for it.
Eleven sorries on the date. Over or under for poker night?
A man who wipes basil leaves one by one is not going to bluff anybody.
No lecture today. Tomorrow: something called Project Habakkuk. We'll pretend we know.
Yossi told Ishai to bring extra cash. Yossi is a mechanic, not a financial adviser.
Tonight apartment 2 becomes a casino. A casino with a fish tank and a china cabinet.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Monday morning. The week has started whether you agreed or not.
Seventeen degrees, a few clouds, and nothing on the roads but everybody.
Caller says her basil has bugs. Madam, everyone's basil has bugs. It's November.
Monday tip: count your change. Count it again. Then trust nobody.
This hour goes out to everyone pretending the weekend isn't over.
Line 88 running on time this morning, which we report as news.
A listener asks: is it rude to bring small notes to a card game? It's rude to bring big ones.
Next up, a song for everybody waiting for Thursday. You know who you are.
Traffic on Herzl is moving. Slowly. With feeling.
Evening on Radio Herzl: soup weather is coming. Get your pot ready.
Someone texted the studio 'what's the opposite of minimalism?' My flat. My flat is.
Good luck to everyone playing cards tonight. And to the people who have to hear about it tomorrow.

zelig: The bugs eat the youngest leaves. So does everything.
Monday. The pigeons don't know. Lucky pigeons.
A man who counts his sorries will one day count his wins.
Cards are only paper. Like money. Like promises.
michal: Monday legs. Never trust Monday legs.
Run club Friday. I'll be there. Probably.
Ten more. Then ten more. Then coffee.
sivan: Incline four, speed nine. Mondays deserve punishment.
Nobody walks on a treadmill. You run or you go home.
Hm. The slow one didn't come this morning.
lior: Chapter fifteen. He goes north. No. Not yet.
The barista leaves on page two hundred. Or doesn't.
Coffee number three. The hero is still apologising.
A nail on a wall where a picture was. Good image. Mine now.
kobi: Monday is a lottery number. Seven. Always seven.
Cards? No. Cards have opinions. Numbers don't.
One beer for Monday. One for Tuesday. In advance.
I'm not drunk, the bar is leaning.

street: ...she said Thursday, which means Sunday, which means never...
...a socket, a whole afternoon, for one socket...
...my son plays cards on Mondays, I don't ask...
...the bus was early and I missed it anyway...
market: ...dish soap and water, it kills them, my mother swore by it...
...two kilos and he wants a discount for being handsome...
...the good tomatoes are finished, these are the brave ones...
...fresh mint, fresh, I cut it this morning with my own hands...
park: ...that duck has lived here longer than me...
...my grandson says pigeons are just city doves, I say they know...
...if the dog pulls, you stop, you don't pull back...
...seventeen degrees and I'm in a coat, I know, I know...
cafe: ...the milk foam is art, I'm not drinking it, I'm photographing it...
...she's quieter this week, the barista, did you notice...
...he's been writing that book since the shekel was new...
...one cappuccino, oat, and don't draw anything on it, I'm sad...

chat.say: Good morning neighbours. Reminder: building fees by Thursday. Cash to Moti, receipts provided.
Cough better. Ishai fed the cats again. Ben-Gurion says thank you. I translate.
Does anyone have dish soap? Not for dishes. Long story.
Card table tonight in apt 2. Quiet please after 22:00. That includes the winners.
Chairs borrowed from the lobby will return tomorrow. Boaz.
The cats are complaining about the new food. They are wrong.
Stair light on the first floor: please press the switch, do not hit it. Thank you.
Who is laughing in apt 2? Sounds like somebody lost. Good night.
